app.title: LifeSim
app.tagline: Live one whole life inside the real historical timeline
app.stageNotice: Playable test build: five regions, births 1950–2026, real WPP mortality and historical geography and currencies. Parents work, fall ill and die; marriage, children, moving and city weights are not modelled yet. The interface is being redesigned as a historical archive (M4-022).

creation.heading: Birth settings

region.randomHint: Drawn only from the five launch regions, weighted by each region's births in the chosen year

year.randomHint: Every year from {{min}} to {{max}} is equally likely

creation.randomRule: Random years are equally likely; the region is weighted by births in the five regions that year.
creation.startHint: Runs on the real WPP life tables and a D-grade rules baseline; the test build will keep being rebalanced.

intro.title: Birth archive
intro.lead: Choose a birth region and year; the simulator registers a new life using the real birth statistics of that year.

sex.hint: Used for birth statistics and sex-specific life tables. This field does not describe gender identity.

play.autoSave: Autosaved in this browser; clearing site data loses it.

status.heading: Status
status.pendingNote: Health, happiness, knowledge, relationships and economy will be derived from the underlying state by M4-016; until then no estimated numbers are shown.

about.heading: What are these?
about.summary: These indicators are derived from the underlying state using D-grade design assumptions, not statistical measurements. They are read-only and do not affect simulation rules.
about.health: Health reflects age and the number of treated and untreated illnesses.
about.happiness: Combines the other indicators, recent experiences and stress; higher stress lowers this value.
about.knowledge: Derived from education, enrollment, aptitude and skills.
about.relationships: Based on relationship quality and everyday social contact.
about.economy: Economy reflects the balance or debt relative to the latest annual income; it does not compare wealth across eras.

saveWriteIssue.heading: Current progress has not been saved
saveWriteIssue.detail: Browser storage is unavailable or full. Your progress is still on this page, but closing or refreshing may lose it. Retry saving or export a backup first.

saveIssue.heading: The previous save could not be loaded
saveIssue.incompatible: This save comes from an older version (different rules or data version), so the current version cannot continue it.
saveIssue.unreadable: This save is damaged or has an invalid format, so the current version cannot read it.
saveIssue.kept: The original save is still kept in this browser and will not be deleted automatically. Download a backup first, then decide whether to clear it.
saveIssue.clear: Clear the save and start over
saveIssue.confirmClear: Click again to confirm the deletion (cannot be undone)

ineligible.not-yet-available: Treatment is not available in this era

time.heading: Time controls
time.finishHint: The remaining major decisions will be made by life principles.

about.heading: About this simulation
about.notPrediction: This is an interactive simulation informed by historical statistics, not a scientific prediction of anyone's fate.
about.historyFixed: Real macro history stays fixed; personal and family outcomes are simulated fiction.
about.notGlobal: Random births are drawn from the five launch regions only, not from the global birth distribution.
about.offline: By default it connects to no server and calls no AI model.

design.lead: Development only: M4-022 colour tokens, archive components and pixel samples. Not part of the production build.
design.sampleValues: Numbers and text on this page are component samples, not simulation results.
design.sampleMajor: After secondary school, decided to apply to university.

offline.unavailable: Offline storage is unavailable in this browser. You can still play online.

offline.updateWhenOnline: Connect to update. You can continue your life offline.

principles.heading: Life principles
principles.hint: Choose what matters in automatic decisions. Values do not need to total 1 and stay fixed for this life.

intervention.heading: Intervention policy
intervention.hint: Change before continuing. This setting determines when you choose. Yearly focus is set in advance under “Yearly focus” below and resolves automatically without pausing.

focus.heading: Yearly focus
focus.ignored: Your focus “{{focus}}” was not available this year, so your life principles decided.
focus.notYet: Not available in the current situation
focus.hint: Applies every year from the next birthday until you change it; in a year where it is not available, your life principles decide. Past years never change.

effects.heading: About the effects
effects.note: Percentages adjust that year's probability of the event, kept within 0–1; stress and social ties use a 0–100 scale and settle at the end of the year. All of these are design assumptions, not statistical findings; focus never changes the risk of death directly.

cohort.heading: Others born that day
cohort.unavailable: Cannot compute: this needs the country data for all five regions. Load them online and try again.

offline.heading: Country data needs a connection
offline.detail: The comparison calculates four more lives across all five regions, so opening it for the first time downloads all five country packs. The app does not pre-cache every country. You are offline or the download failed; reconnect and choose Retry.

failed.heading: Calculation failed
failed.detail: This comparison could not be calculated, but your life is not affected and you can keep playing. Choose Retry; if it keeps failing, carry on and open it again later.

four.heading: Four others born the same second
four.disclosure: Four other people were born on your birthday; their regions are drawn with weights from the five regions’ birth counts for that year. They live automatically by the life principles in the same engine and are only advanced to your current year. What happened to them is simulated, not a statistic.

survival.heading: Survival curve
survival.title: Share still alive: born {{year}} in {{pack}}, both sexes combined
survival.scenarioFrom: Scenario from age {{age}} (grade D): once birth year + age passes 2100, the curve holds the 2100 column constant.
survival.legendPeriod: Observed / WPP projected period table (grade B)
survival.dataMissing: Data missing: the life table has no usable value after age {{age}}, so the curve stops at {{age}}.
survival.disclosure: Evidence grade B: UN WPP 2024 single-age life table (both sexes combined), covering up to 2100. Method: the yearly period life table approximates the birth cohort, so the step from age a to a + 1 uses q(a) from the year birth year + a. Once birth year + a passes 2100 the curve holds the 2100 column constant and is labelled a grade D scenario; ages above 100 are treated as q = 1. This curve comes only from the life table, not from the four simulated lives above.
